title: Sparkplug: transactional admin task runner for safe runbook execution
creator: Diego Martinez
description: Build Sparkplug: a lightweight transactional task runner that converts human runbooks into verified, idempotent operator tasks. Goals: (1) allow SREs and support engineers to author steps in YAML/markdown and execute them as safe, auditable tasks; (2) provide dry-run and simulation modes for validation; (3) provide automatic rollback / compensating actions for multi-step operations; (4) integrate with the Console for per-run tracing, cost/latency telemetry, and canary deploys. This ticket covers the MVP execution engine and the admin CLI integration for staging and canary runs. The runner must be agentless (operator-triggered API calls), support plugins for safety checks, and emit standardized telemetry events for post-mortem analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Author a runbook in YAML and convert to a Sparkplug DAG without manual edits
Execute DAG in dry-run mode with no side effects and a validation report
Run a normal execution that supports transactional semantics: either all critical steps succeed or compensating steps are run
All runs produce an immutable audit record (run_id) with per-step logs visible in Console
Support canary target selection (staging subset) and automatic abort on health checks
Telemetry emitted to metrics pipeline with event schema sparkplug.run.{started,step.succeeded,step.failed,aborted}

steps_taken: Built YAML->DAG transformer that recognizes step types: api_call, sql, shell, sleep, manual-approval
Implemented dry-run mode that validates preconditions and simulates API responses using recorded samples
Added optimistic locking / run-lease to prevent concurrent conflicting runs against same resource
Wired telemetry events to the metrics pipeline and created an initial dashboard prototype
Created a minimal compensating-step DSL and validator to enable automatic rollback
